note: acq. by Papaya Global, 2022 (the CMS). Wikipedia 'Azimo': Series A and B funding from investors including e.ventures. eVentures led the ~$1M seed (Sep 2013), matching CMS 'Early 2013'; the only earlier money was £300K from angels (Jan 2013). Next priced round: $10M Series A led by Greycroft (Mar 2014), e.ventures participating.

data.ai (formerly App Annie); acq. by Sensor Tower, 2024 (the firm's CMS). App Annie's own release (2012-08-14): $6M Series B led by Greycroft with e.ventures participating; the Series A (2011) was IDG alone, so the entry is Series B, matching CMS 'Early 2012'. Round labels after 2013 vary by source (TechCrunch calls the Jan 2015 IVP round Series D; IVP's own row calls it Series E).

acq. by Yahoo, December 2005 (bvcapital.com 'Portfolio Company Del.icio.us Acquired by Yahoo'). USV's book reads the April 2005 round as the seed. TechCrunch's 2005 profile lists BV Capital among the April 2005 seed investors (USV's own post dates the close to 2005-04-14; amount only 'rumored'). Acquired by Yahoo eight months later, so there was no priced Series A. Pre-2006 row.

The CMS's 'Exit 2023' is the firm's own exit (a sale of its stake); Graylog itself operates. HTGF's release (2013-11-25): TORCH GmbH (Graylog's company) closed a seed round from e.ventures, HTGF, Hasso Plattner Ventures and Atlantic Capital Partners, with a Christian Leybold quote; no lead or amount given. Next priced round: $2.5M led by Mercury Fund (Feb 2015, not labelled); e.ventures is not named in 2015 or among the 2021 existing investors, consistent with the CMS 'Exit 2023' being a stake sale. Graylog operates.

funding_rounds.lead: Silver Lake Waterman, Piper Sandler Merchant Banking, Harbert Growth Partners

note: acq. by Axel Springer, 2011 (the firm's CMS). eVenture Capital Partners (Otto Group's VC arm, Andreas Haug; merged into e.ventures in 2012) led kaufDA's first institutional round, Aug 2009, 'mittleren einstelligen Millionenbetrag' (mid single-digit EUR millions, no exact figure); TechCrunch (2011) calls it the Series A; TechCrunch (2009-08-21) says eVenture led it and took 18%. Earlier 2008 money came from angels only. Note the firm lineage here is the eVCP side, not BV Capital.

acq. by Accel-KKR, 2020 (the firm's CMS). TechCrunch (2012-01-24) and Recurly's own blog: $6M Series A led by BV Capital with seed investors Polaris, Harrison Metal and FreeStyle; the $1.6M seed (Aug 2010, led by Polaris) had no BV money. CMS 'Early 2011' is the close year.

Vuze, Inc. (formerly Azureus, the BitTorrent client); Wikipedia: a later round 'led by NEA, with existing investors Redpoint Ventures, Greycroft Partners, BV Capital'; BV Capital's entry round and the company's later state are not established. | Vuze, Inc. (formerly Azureus, the BitTorrent client); Wikipedia: a later round 'led by NEA, with existing investors Redpoint Ventures, Greycroft Partners, BV Capital'; BV Capital's entry round and the company's later state are not established. The company wound down after the client was sold on (aligned with the Redpoint row, which holds Vuze and its predecessor Azureus). TechCrunch (Dec 2007) gives the full history: $2M Series A with BV Capital (Azureus Inc., 2006; BV presumably sole/lead), $12M Series B with Redpoint, Greycroft, BV Capital and Mohn (announced 2006-12-03), $20M Series C led by NEA. The exit is weakly sourced (Wikipedia 'citation needed'); Redpoint's row reads defunct, so the status needs a ruling.

acq. by Yahoo, 2000 (stock, ~$432M); the BV-era position came through ONElist, which merged into eGroups in 1999 (Wikipedia 'Headline (company)'). bvcapital.com 'eGroups (YHOO)' 2008-2010. The firm's entry was ONElist's only preferred round (Series A), a joint CMGI @Ventures / Bertelsmann Ventures investment announced 1999-01-11; the round name comes from the eGroups S-1 (Mar 2000), whose related-party table shows Bertelsmann Ventures holding 2,876,371 eGroups Series C shares (the exchanged ONElist Series A) and 680,272 Series D, $8.6M paid in total. The press release names the firm but not the round word, so the quote rule is met only across the two sources. Pre-2006 row.

IPO NYSE 2018; taken private by Coupang, January 2024. The CMS lists e.ventures' early entry (2011) and a Japan buyback exit (2016). e.ventures ('eVenture Capital Partners') joined the $18M round led by Index announced Jan 2012 (CMS close 2011). The Series B label is inferred: Advent's $4.5M in 2010 was the first round and Advent's partner calls the 2013 Condé Nast round 'effectively a Series C'; no page found that prints 'Series B' for the 2012 round. The CMS 'Early (Japan) 2014' is a separate Farfetch Japan position.

Codefied Inc. does business as Housecall Pro (Form Ds 2013-2022, Gieselmann director; merged). HQ Denver (the firm's CMS and the 2022 Form D, 4180 Wynkoop Street); founded in San Diego. TechCrunch (2014-01-16): Housecall 'has raised $1.5 million from investors, including e.ventures', which matches the first Form D (Codefied Inc., first sale 2013-07-26, $1.5M, Thomas Gieselmann of e.ventures as director) and CMS 'Early 2013'. The Seed label is inferred (first outside money for a six-person startup); no page names the round. The next rounds (Form D $7.6M in 2015, $11.0M in 2017) carry no series label in any source found, so the next priced round is uncited.

funding_rounds.lead: Permira Growth Opportunities, Vista Credit Partners

note: acq. by eBay, 2013 (the firm's CMS). e.ventures came in as a new backer in the $3.2M round of Oct 2012 (CMS 'Early 2012'), alongside Notion Capital and existing investors UPS Strategic Enterprise Fund and Hummingbird. No source gives series labels ('six separate fundraisings', total $8.69M by exit); Series A is inferred as the first institutional VC round. Acquired by eBay in Oct 2013 before any later priced round.

acq. by VIVA Wine Group, 2021 (the firm's CMS). eVenture Capital Partners (Otto's VC arm, merged into e.ventures in 2012; Christian Leybold) took 10% of the joint Wine in Black / Vicampo company in 2011 alongside Passion Capital, before the two split in 2012 (e.ventures kept 10% of Vicampo). No source names the 2011 round; Seed is inferred (first institutional money, company founded 2011). Later rounds (Sep 2013 'in Millionenhöhe', Mar 2015 EUR 3.75M, 2016 EUR 5.3M with Burda; about EUR 10M raised in total by Feb 2017) carry no series label, so the next priced round is uncited.

acq. by Oracle, 2014 (~$400M reported). BV Capital lists it from 2010 (bvcapital.com /portfolio/show/bluekai). No round names BV Capital. The Feb 2010 Series C release lists only GGV (lead) plus existing investors Redpoint and Battery, and says the prior $13.7M came in two rounds from Redpoint and Battery; bvcapital.com lists BlueKai from 2010, so BV's stake was likely a secondary purchase or an unannounced later tranche.

Made.com entered administration in November 2022 and its brand, website and IP were bought by Next plc: an asset sale out of insolvency, acquired with a successor note (COLLECTION.md s6). Listed by Andreas Haug on his team page; no e.ventures round was located in press, so membership rests on the firm's own listing (medium). No round naming e.ventures (or eVenture Capital Partners) was found: the 2010 seed (Hoberman, PROfounders, John Hunt, Jaina Capital), the 2012 £6M Series B (Level Equity, PROfounders) and the 2018 £40M round (Partech, Level Equity, Eight Roads) all list other investors. A possible link: founder Ning Li co-founded MyFab, and both MyFab and Hoberman's mydeco were eVCP/BV Capital portfolio companies, but that is not a Made.com round. Membership rests only on Andreas Haug's team-page listing.

nCircle (vulnerability management), acq. by Tripwire, 2013. No funding round naming BV Capital (or Bertelsmann Ventures) was found; nCircle's rounds predate 2006 and are not in Google News. The firm's own 2008 pages list nCircle under Communications Software and say Thomas Gieselmann 'observes at nCircle' (a board observer seat), which confirms membership but not the round.

acq. by Best Buy, 2007 (bvcapital.com 'Best Buy Acquires Speakeasy'). No funding round naming BV Capital or Bertelsmann Ventures was found; Speakeasy's venture rounds predate Google News coverage and Wikipedia gives none. Membership rests on bvcapital.com's own 'Speakeasy (BBY)' portfolio page and its reposted Best Buy release (purchase price ~$97M, 1.2x 2006 revenue). Pre-2006 row.

acq. by Twilio, 2020 ($3.2B; Twilio's resale S-3ASR of 2020-11 in the full-text sweep). The only round naming e.ventures is the April 2019 Series D, where CFO.com calls it a 'new investor'. But Twilio's resale S-3ASR shows 96% of the e.ventures shares in BV eVenture Fund II (the early-stage fund) and only 19,817 in e.ventures Growth II, which backs the CMS 'Early 2013' entry; that 2013 round (after the $600K NEA/General Catalyst seed, before Accel's ~$15M 2014 round) was not found. Entry left null rather than record the Series D, which is likely only the growth fund's entry.

acq. by Disney, 2014. Listed by Mathias Schilling on his team page; no e.ventures round was located in press (Greycroft, e.ventures' frequent co-investor, was in the 2012 round), so membership rests on the firm's own listing (medium). No round naming e.ventures/BV Capital was found. TechCrunch puts total funding at $70M by Sep 2013, of which $62M was the Series C (Time Warner-led Dec 2012 tranche plus the Sep 2013 tranche), so about $8M came in earlier rounds, including Greycroft's $1.5M in April 2011. The firm's site carried a Maker logo by Feb 2012, so the entry is likely one of those 2011-2012 pre-C rounds, but no page ties the firm to one; neither Series C tranche names e.ventures. The firm's own site carried a Maker logo by February 2012 (read by the research agent on an archive capture), supporting the team-page listing.

basis: Sale consideration (COLLECTION.md s1; Point Nine's share-swap ruling of 2026-09-26; decisions.md R2): every round the firm was in went into Deposit Solutions (Hamburg, founded 2011: the July 2016 EUR 15M round, the 2018 $100M round), which merged into Raisin in June 2021 by share swap (Finextra). Raisin's own rounds carry no e.ventures money (the 2015 Series B was Ribbit and Index). The firm's CMS lists the merged 'Raisin' with Deposit Solutions' founder Tim Sievers among its founders. Deposit Solutions is the member (recall addition).
